=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:`_is_permanent_memory_push_failure` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The rate-limit/abuse exclusion runs on the whole stderr after only URLs are removed. A repo slug in the `remote: Permission to <owner>/rate-limiter.git denied` line matches, so a 403 permission denial is classified as temporary.
  WHY: A repo named `rate-limiter` or `abuse-tools` gets all 16 retries with backoff, fetch and rebase. The suggested fix is to remove the `permission to \S+ denied` span before the rate-limit search and add a test pairing that line with a 403 line.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS: scripts/ai_memory_lib.py, rate-limit exclusion; remove the permission span and add a classifier test (3-4 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1

- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:3286-3305 (also 3275-3278) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When stderr has both a 403 and a `Permission to <repo> denied` line whose slug contains `rate-limit`, the failure is still misclassified as temporary. For example, `The requested URL returned error: 403\nremote: Permission to o/rate-limiter.git denied to some-bot.` returns False.
  WHY: Pushes to repos named with `rate-limit` or `abuse` burn the full 16-attempt retry budget on a deterministic denial. The widened `abuse` regex also treats a non-URL string containing `abuse`, next to a 403 and an auth-failure pattern, as temporary.
- tests/test_ai_memory_push_retry_backoff.py:~519 (hardening)

  WHY: The suggested fix is two permanent cases, one with a `rate-limit` slug and one with `abuse` next to a credential failure (about 6 lines).
- scripts/ai_memory_lib.py:3290-3291 (hardening)
  PROBLEM: The docstring omits that URLs are stripped before the rate-limit or abuse match.
  WHY: The suggested fix is to change the wording to "non-URL text" (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1 (the section also gave a score of 2).
